name: Housing & Urban Development Corporation Ltd
title: Housing & Urban Development Corporation Ltd - 540530 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: HUDCO guides FY27 disbursement of about INR65,000 crore and a INR3 lakh crore loan book by 2030, with spreads held near 2%, but the call offers no hard supply-side evidence and sanctions are being chased with lengthy project timelines.

summary.headline: HUDCO guides FY27 disbursement of about INR65,000 crore and a INR3 lakh crore loan book by 2029-30, with spreads held near 2%.
summary.overview: Management skipped the headline numbers and focused on policy tailwinds (urban challenge fund, bankable projects) and the pipeline. FY27 disbursement target is about INR65,000 crore against about INR5,000 crore achieved last year, with borrowing plan of about INR70,000 crore approved. Two June MoUs (Gujarat and Bihar, each above INR1 lakh crore) were presented as pipeline, with sanctions expected to start this quarter. Management reiterated a spread of around 2% and NIM of around 3%, though an analyst cited Q1 spread near 1.8%, and said compression is due to fast growth and should reverse by Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Lower due to Board decision not to create DTL on special reserve

financial_highlights.value: about INR20,000 crore; INR4,000 crore+ received in Q1

segments.name: Urban infrastructure / sustainable finance
segments.commentary: Q1 sanctions included ring roads, expressways, irrigation, water grid, industrial corridors, power generation/distribution, Telangana urban infra and water supply/sewage. Management said water and sanitation are the core sustainable-finance focus, aligned with AMRUT and MoHUA priorities.

segments.name: Housing
segments.commentary: Housing portfolio is shrinking because states are not bringing counterpart funding under PMAY; housing lending is priced around MCLR of about 8.6%.

segments.name: Private sector / PPP project finance
segments.commentary: New PPP project finance division; 2 projects sanctioned in Q1 worth about INR6,000-7,000 crore. Disbursement expected to start in the latter part of FY27. No internal target set.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target about INR65,000 crore; borrowing plan about INR70,000 crore approved by Board.
Loan book target of INR3 lakh crore by 2030 (FY30); FY28 not planned, with mid-FY28 review and market disclosure if course correction needed.
Spread to be maintained around 2% and NIM around 3%; spread expected to reflect in Q3 as Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 disbursements capitalise.

Gujarat and Bihar MoUs (each above INR1 lakh crore; combined about INR2 lakh crore): sanctions to start in Q2 FY27 for Gujarat, with works in Q4 FY27 or earlier; MoUs valid 5 years, disbursement over around 5 years.

FX borrowing: RBI forex window tie-up of about USD2 billion (about USD700 million drawn), all-in cost about 5.5-6.5% including hedging, with ECB share possibly rising from about 10% to 20% of borrowings.
capex_capacity: Gujarat MoU: metro, RRTS, Olympic/Commonwealth Games infrastructure (Commonwealth Games Ahmedabad 2030), highways; sanctions expected this quarter.
Bihar MoU: 12 satellite towns; Bihar road projects of about INR21,000 crore identified; tourism, metro and digital parks under discussion.
Repayments of INR15,000-16,000 crore expected over remaining quarters of FY27.
demand_pricing: Analyst cited Q1 spread near 1.8%; management attributed compression to accelerated growth and expects 2% spread to return by Q3.
Competition for state financing from NABARD, NaBFID and commercial banks has pushed rates down, per management.
Borrowing mix: about 70% domestic (bank loans and bonds), about 10% ECB currently; ECB could rise to 20% over next five years.
Management said yield is not split between urban infra and housing; rates are sector-specific.

qa_highlights.question: What is the short-term foreign exposure and what are the lending rates/portfolio yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said short-term foreign currency loans have been retired and over 99% is 5-year borrowing. Spread guided around 2%, NIM around 3%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FX accounting loss issue behind us, and how will the Gujarat and Bihar MoUs translate into sanctions?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance director said no FCNRs maturing in FY27 or FY28 except USD200 million maturing in 2028, which is secured; no forex losses foreseen this year. Gujarat sanctions expected this quarter; Bihar has 12 satellite towns and road projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR3 lakh crore loan book guidance conservative given MoU visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed partly, citing land acquisition, social and political issues and state compliance before contract award; said projects typically complete within 5 years, so 5-year horizon is preferred.

qa_highlights.question: What is the internal target for private sector / PPP book?
qa_highlights.answer: No target set for private sanctions; approach is case-by-case with good entities and strong concessions. UCF PPP projects in water, desalination, drainage and sewage are expected; UCF gives 50% VGF.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 disbursement and repayment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 disbursement about INR65,000 crore; total repayments about INR20,000 crore, with INR4,000 crore+ received in Q1 and INR15,000-16,000 crore expected in the remaining quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the forex window borrowing size and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: USD2 billion tie-up is the minimum; all-in cost including hedging about 5.5-6.5%, as RBI covers most hedging and HUDCO pays about 1.5%.

risks_watch: Spread: Q1 spread near 1.8% per analyst vs 2% guidance; watch Q2 and Q3 for recovery as higher-yield disbursements capitalise.
Execution risk on the INR3 lakh crore 2030 loan book and the MoU-linked sanctions, given land, political and state-compliance delays.
Gross NPA of about INR1,600 crore, of which about INR1,100 crore sits in NCLT (mostly pre-2013 projects); management targets resolution in FY27.
Rising ECB share (up to 20%) increases FX exposure, dependent on forex window availability and cost.
Housing book shrinking as states do not provide counterpart funding; watch housing sanctions.
Tax rate change from no DTL on special reserve (effective rate about 20.6%) affects comparability.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, policy and pipeline, but evasive on specifics such as segment yield splits, private-sector targets and the spread gap. Management repeatedly deferred to the Director of Finance on FX, tax and repayment numbers.
key_quotes: So, we have repeatedly advised the market that there will not be any target for the private sector sanctions or the disbursement.
So, in the next year, we have not planned, but 2030, we have planned a loan book of INR3 lakh crores, and I'm very sure that we will be achieving that INR 3 lakh crores loan book.
Yes, I think we will be maintaining this 2% spread. I think it will easily come to us.
The USD2 billion will be the minimum figure.
